title: The Largest Triangle That Can Be Made From Three Sticks

concept.title: Sort the sticks: if three sticks cannot make a triangle, the biggest one can be dropped
body: Choose three of the given sticks to make a triangle with a **positive area**, and make the **perimeter** (the sum of the three lengths) as large as possible. Three lengths `a <= b <= c` make a triangle exactly when the two shorter ones are together **longer** than the longest: `a + b > c`. If no three sticks work, the answer is 0. For the sticks `2 1 2` the answer is 5; for `1 2 1` it is 0 (1 + 1 = 2 is not enough).

Sort the sticks from the **longest** to the shortest and look at three **neighbours** `x >= y >= z` in this order. If `y + z > x`, they make a triangle, and it is the best one: any other triangle uses sticks that are not longer in the sorted order, so its perimeter is not bigger. If `y + z <= x`, then `x` is too long for any pair of shorter sticks (the biggest sum of two sticks smaller than `x` is `y + z`), so `x` is useless in any triangle: **drop it** and continue with the next three.

body.code:
a.sort(reverse=True)
answer = 0
for i in range(len(a) - 2):
    if a[i + 1] + a[i + 2] > a[i]:
        answer = a[i] + a[i + 1] + a[i + 2]
        break
print(answer)

body: Only neighbours need to be checked, thanks to this argument: for a fixed longest stick, the best pair of the other two is the pair just after it in the sorted order. Sorting costs O(n log n) and the scan O(n). The perimeter can reach 3 * 10^9, so 64-bit numbers are used.

statement: `n` sticks with the given lengths are available. Choose three of them that form a triangle with a positive area, so that the perimeter is as large as possible. Print the largest perimeter, or 0 if no triangle can be made.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of sticks.
The second line has `n` numbers: the lengths of the sticks.
hints: Three lengths a <= b <= c form a triangle exactly when a + b > c.
Sort in descending order and test three neighbours.
The first triple that works gives the largest perimeter.

explanation: The lengths are sorted in descending order; for three neighbours x >= y >= z the triple makes a triangle when y + z > x, and the first such triple is the best, because a stick that is too long for its two neighbours is too long for any pair of shorter sticks.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

a.sort(reverse=True)
answer = 0
for i in range(n - 2):
    if a[i + 1] + a[i + 2] > a[i]:
        answer = a[i] + a[i + 1] + a[i + 2]
        break
print(answer)
